steps.step: Create a project plan and estimate how many scholarships can potentially be provided that year.
steps.trigger: The annual scholarship program needs to start.
steps.rule: Scholarships are offered for up to Greenbelt.

steps.step: Create the scholarship task in OSI's ClickUp intake board, move it into project accepted, create the project dashboard task, and create a Teams folder with resources for the project.
steps.trigger: The potential scholarship funding and project plan are identified.
steps.system: OSI's ClickUp intake board; ClickUp project dashboard; Teams
steps.rule: The task is moved into project accepted; no MOU is drafted for this process.
steps.waitTime: Moved into project accepted fairly quickly

steps.step: Plan the marketing timeline, application window, evaluation period, anticipated awardees, and potential class dates with OSI and the DES program manager.
steps.trigger: The project task is accepted and the annual timeline needs to be set.
steps.who: OSI, the financial person or OSI initiative support, and the DES program manager
steps.rule: The class timing needs to align with the scholarship timeline.
steps.waitTime: Part of the roughly 2-month planning period

steps.step: Create a communication plan and update images, flyers, banners, emails, process maps, the website, and that year's frequently asked questions document.
steps.trigger: The overarching plan and timeline are agreed upon.
steps.handsOnTime: About 6 to 10 hours for updating resources

steps.step: Review the previous year's KualiBuild form, validate whether its fields are still relevant, make changes as needed, and publish the form for applicants.
steps.trigger: The application materials are being prepared for the next applicant set.
steps.rule: Applicants fill out all required fields.

steps.step: Schedule and prepare the live informational session, including creating the Zoom meeting and the process for sending people information about it.
steps.trigger: The application window is being prepared.
steps.handsOnTime: Included in 10 to 20 hours of administrative overhead for questions and delivering the informational session

steps.step: Contact people who served on the previous year's committee, coordinate their availability, and block evaluation dates on their calendars.
steps.trigger: An evaluation committee is needed for the application review.
steps.who: OSI and potential evaluation committee members
steps.whatGoesWrong: There are "a lot of emails back and forth trying to coordinate folks".

steps.step: Publicize that the scholarship window will be available through the website, email, Blink website, Teams channels, and newsletters.
steps.trigger: The application window is ready to be announced.
steps.system: OSI website; email; Blink website; Teams channels; newsletters
steps.handsOnTime: Included in the 6 to 10 hours for updating resources

steps.step: Review the scholarship information and think about the process to work on during the class.
steps.trigger: The interested person hears about the scholarship through the communication channels.
steps.system: OSI website; KualiBuild form; emails; Blink website; Teams channels; newsletters; Zoom
steps.rule: The application window is typically open for about a month.

steps.step: Document the process idea in a Word document or notes and review it with the supervisor before applying.
steps.trigger: The applicant has identified a process to work on during the class.
steps.rule: The supervisor is expected to support classwork and project work during work hours.

steps.step: Click the KualiBuild link, fill out the required fields about the applicant, supervisor, process, data, and pain points, and submit the application.
steps.trigger: The applicant has reviewed the process with the supervisor and is ready to apply.
steps.rule: The form contains required fields and asks for process details, data, and pain points.

steps.step: Receive the submitted application notification and complete the supervisor application step by acknowledging awareness, giving a recommendation, and addressing support for classwork and project time.
steps.trigger: KualiBuild automatically sends a notification after the applicant submits the form.
steps.rule: The supervisor gives a recommendation and is expected to support classwork and project time during work hours.

steps.step: Close the KualiBuild form after the application window and review and score the submissions using the rubric and evaluation guide.
steps.trigger: The application window closes and the supervisor steps are available to the scholarship committee.
steps.rule: The committee reviews and scores submissions against a rubric and evaluation guide.
steps.handsOnTime: About 10 hours per committee member, with up to 5 or 6 committee members

steps.step: Conduct a final review of the scored submissions to consider whether the potential awards include different VC areas, project types, and campus areas rather than the same portions of campus or the same problems.
steps.trigger: The initial pass has scored all submissions.
steps.rule: The committee considers the overall set of awards and the number it is able to award.

steps.step: Agree on how many scholarships can be awarded and send customized award or non-award emails.
steps.trigger: The committee agrees on the number of scholarships it can award.
steps.rule: Award and non-award language is preset in the KualiBuild form and is believed to be automated.

steps.step: If awarded, set up a student account and register for the class term through the DES program manager.
steps.trigger: The awardee receives the award notification.
steps.system: DES program manager's registration process; student account; class registration

steps.step: Attend an informational meeting with the awardees, OSI, and the DES program manager to build community, ask questions, and understand what is needed moving forward.
steps.trigger: Awardees receive the award notification and enrollment direction.
steps.who: Awardees, OSI, and the DES program manager
steps.system: Meeting with awardees, OSI, and DES program manager
steps.rule: Awardees are expected to let OSI know how the project went and can rely on OSI as a resource.
steps.whatGoesWrong: "Not a lot of people take us up on that" resource and support opportunity.

steps.step: Take the class and work on the process project, with time needed for both classwork and project work.
steps.trigger: The awardee registers for the class term.
steps.who: Awardee, with supervisor support and OSI available as a resource
steps.system: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies; supervisor; OSI
steps.rule: The supervisor is expected to help block off time for the class and project.
steps.waitTime: Follow-up occurs over about 3 to 9 months after the application and review period

steps.step: Deliver the final presentation and send the presentation and related project details to OSI.
steps.trigger: The awardee finishes the project and delivers the final presentation.
steps.rule: Awardees should send the final presentation and related details to OSI.
steps.waitTime: Typically 3 to 6 months later; overall follow-up is described as 3 to 9 months

steps.step: Meet with OSI to discuss the process changes, estimate potential financial impacts, and record the project name, financial outcomes, and calculation details in the impact savings tracker and dashboards.
steps.trigger: OSI receives the final presentation and related project details.
steps.system: OSI Excel impact savings tracker; OSI dashboards; meeting with OSI
steps.rule: OSI estimates conservatively, validates data as much as possible, and selects the lower end of a range when there is a range.
steps.whatGoesWrong: Candidates are "often not very skilled" at measuring financial impacts and may feel they do not know how to make the calculation or do not have enough data to validate it.
